newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan mine firm seeks listing on Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan mine firm seeks listing on Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Athi River Mining Ltd (ARM), a Kenyan cement, chemicals and mineral manufacturing concern, on Thursday announced plans for an initial public offering on the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE).

"The issue of new shares will provide additional capital for its expansion programme to meet the growing demand for its cement and other products in Kenya and in export markets," ARM Chairman Alan Pickering said in a statement.
Upon listing ARM will become the third cement manufacturing concern on the Nairobi bourse. The others are Bamburi Cement Limited and East African Portland Cement.
In Thursday trading, Bamburi eased to 40 from 40.50 on Wednesday but East African Portland Cement rose to 31.50 from 30.75.
Its listing will boost the Nairobi bourse's potential as an avenue for raising capital by industrial companies. Brokers said that avenue was not fully exploited in Kenya.
The ARM share issue will be managed by Commercial Bank of Africa while Shah, Munge & Partners, Kestrel Capital (East Africa) and Ashbu Securities will be the sponsoring brokers.
ARM began operations in 1973 by Harjivandas Paunrana with an initial capital outlay of 75,000 shillings ($1,390) and an overdraft of 10,000 shillings.
The firm boasted a profit of 28.14 million shillings ($0.5 million) after tax in the year ended December 31, 1996 compared to 18.779 million shillings the previous year.

A senior official from the company said the profits earned in 1996 were from five months of cement sales as their cement production began in August and said projected 1997 profit after tax would be about 68 million shillings.

Harjivandas and his son Pradeep Paunrana own 80 percent of the company. They are not selling their shares but with the creation of additional shares, their percentage shareholding is expected to decrease, the official said.
The ARM public flotation will start in around a month after relevant approvals from the Nairobi Stock Exchange and the regulatory Capital Markets Authority.
The company did not say how much money it planned to raise or what company percentage would be sold.
ARM will become the 61st company listed on the bourse.
